sentences.text: Tsagantegia was a medium-sized ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, estimated to reach lengths of 6 to 7 meters and weigh between 1 and 4 tons.
The only known specimen is a very partial individual consisting solely of a skull, which features an elongated snout and flattened facial osteoderms that differ greatly from other ankylosaurs.
Unlike other Asian ankylosaurs, the cranial ornamentation of this animal is amorphous and flattened rather than a mosaic of polygons.
No additional remains of Tsagantegia longicranialis have been found or mentioned in scientific literature since its description.
Palatal comparisons show Tsagantegia had a shovel-shaped mouth, unlike the wide rectangular snout of the contemporary Talarurus.
The skull remained unresearched until it was formally described by Russian paleontologist Tatiana Tumanova in 1993 as a new genus and species, Tsagantegia longicranialis.
The genus name refers to the Tsagan-Teg locality, while the species name means "long-skulled" in Latin.

Comparisons with Talarurus suggest Tsagantegia was a browser herbivore, whereas Talarurus was a grazer, as morphological differences indicate Tsagantegia filled the niche of a browsing herbivore while Talarurus was a grazer.

Tsagantegia shared its habitat with various dinosaurs and non-dinosaurs including theropods like Achillobator and Alectrosaurus, the ankylosaurid Talarurus, marginocephalians like Amtocephale and Graciliceratops, the hadrosauroid Gobihadros, and the sauropod Erketu.
Tsagantegia is classified within the family Ankylosauridae, belongs to the parent group Ankylosaurinae, and is a member of the class Ornithischia.

A 2012 analysis found that Tsagantegia was closely related to Pinacosaurus and Shamosaurus, though it is debated whether Tsagantegia belongs to the subfamily Shamosaurinae or is a basal member of Ankylosaurinae.
The type species of the genus Tsagantegia is Tsagantegia longicranialis.

The age of the Bayan Shireh Formation, where Tsagantegia was found, is confirmed to be between 92 and 86 million years ago, while Tsagantegia lived from the Cenomanian to the Santonian, approximately 100.5 to 83.6 million years ago.

The environment where Tsagantegia lived was semi-arid with large rivers and lakes, as caliche layers indicate a semi-arid climate while fluvial and lacustrine sediments suggest the presence of large rivers and lakes.
Fossil fruit remains found at Bor Guvé and Khara Khutul suggest the presence of angiosperm plants in the area.
